meta.description:
This work center encompasses the consolidated administrative and command support functions for 943 RQG/MSF. This Job Safety Training Outline (JSTO) applies to personnel assigned to strictly administrative sections, specifically including the Commander's Support Staff (CSS), Chaplain Corps, Equal Opportunity (EO), Training, Public Affairs (PA), Military & Family Readiness, and Command Staff.

Operations are conducted entirely within a standard office and briefing environment. Primary duties involve computer operation, document processing, personnel counseling, public communication, meeting facilitation, and general administrative coordination. The occupational risk level is inherently low. Potential hazards are limited to routine office safety concerns, such as ergonomic strain, slips, trips, falls, and basic facility emergency egress. Because personnel do not engage in industrial operations or handle hazardous materials, no specialized safety training is required beyond Initial Safety Training and baseline work center familiarization.

In the event that a person (military and/or civilian technician) is injured, the following procedures apply. Immediately notify your supervisor if possible and/or call the Wing Fire Department at 911(from an on-base land line) or 228-3333. The Fire Department will respond with paramedics/EMT’s that are on shift at all times. They have the capability to treat, evaluate and recommend further medical attention. If further medical attention is needed, an off-base ambulance may be called and/or you may be able to seek other transportation to an off-base medical provider.
meta.evacuationRoute: Exit Buildings 5426 or 5434 using the nearest and safest available exit. Personnel must quickly proceed to the designated muster point located in the parking lot northeast of the buildings, commonly known as the TDY parking lot. Once gathered in the TDY parking lot, all personnel must immediately report to their respective section chiefs or designated representatives to conduct physical accountability. Section representatives will then consolidate the roll call and report their status to the Command Staff or On-Scene Commander. Personnel must remain in the TDY parking lot and await further instructions from emergency responders or leadership before attempting to re-enter the facilities.
meta.shelterInPlace: The primary shelter location inside Building 5434, or proceed to the designated secondary shelter location in Building 5426, Room 111, if the primary facility is inaccessible or unsafe.
meta.activeShooterMethods:
1. RUN - Have an escape plan, leave belongings, and Keep hands visible
2. HIDE	- Hide out of shooter's view, Block entry/lock doors, DO NOT attempt to move wounded personnel.
3. FIGHT- LAST RESORT

As a reminder, notifications of an active shooter event are divided into three stages:
LOCKDOWN, STAY PUT, and ALL CLEAR
meta.adverseWeatherShelter: The primary shelter location inside Building 5434, or proceed to the designated secondary shelter location in Building 5426, Room 111, if the primary facility is inaccessible or unsafe.
meta.fireEquipmentNotes: Both Buildings 5426 and 5434 are equipped with automated wet-pipe sprinkler systems and manual fire alarm pull stations that are clearly marked and located throughout the facilities. For immediate fire suppression, Building 5426 is equipped with two fire extinguishers: one is located in the main hallway near the HVAC cutoff switch, and the second is mounted in the Heritage Room. Building 5434 also houses two fire extinguishers: one is located immediately adjacent to the main entrance, and the other is located in the Training Area. Personnel are not equipped with, nor do these administrative spaces require, automated external defibrillators (AEDs) or chemical eyewash stations.
meta.trafficSafetyNotes:
All personnel must exercise heightened situational awareness when commuting to and from work due to unique local traffic conditions in the Tucson metropolitan area 
 . Tucson roadways frequently experience congestion, aggressive driving, and seasonal hazards such as flash flooding and low visibility during the summer monsoon season. Additionally, extreme daytime temperatures in the local area pose a risk of rapid vehicle overheating and tire blowouts 
 . To ensure safety and minimize delays, personnel must plan their commutes around daily peak gate traffic at Davis-Monthan AFB 
 . All base installation gates experience heavy congestion and significant delays during morning inbound rushes from 0600 to 0800, and again during afternoon outbound rushes from 1500 to 1700 
 . Personnel are highly encouraged to practice defensive driving, strictly adhere to posted base speed limits, and utilize hands-free mobile devices exclusively while operating vehicles
